title: Xanthe and the Ledger
premise: In 1917, Edmund Thackeray, a battlefield nurse who records in a private ledger the names of soldiers erased from official reports, is evacuated to a coastal English town where a zealous census taker begins asking questions about the unregistered wounded sheltering at the convalescent house. When orders arrive to move the patients out ahead of a German naval raid, Edmund discovers there is one berth too few on the evacuation boat — and the census taker's records could save or condemn the very people Edmund has sworn to remember. Forced to choose between the truth of the ledger and the loyalty owed to a found family, Edmund ultimately gives up their own place aboard, entrusting the ledger to the youngest patient, and survives the raid ashore to rebuild the household as an officially recognized sanctuary, its names finally spoken aloud.
about_author: Noor Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence in coastal county records offices. They write historical fiction about the people official paperwork forgot.

chapters.title: What the Orders Omit
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At a dressing station near Ypres, Edmund records in a hidden ledger the names of dying privates whose deaths officers leave off reports. When the station receives evacuation orders, Edmund must decide what can be carried — and smuggles the ledger out in a stretcher kit. Emotional beat: quiet defiance born of grief.

chapters.title: The House at Saltmere
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Reassigned to a crumbling convalescent house on the Kent coast run by the formidable Mrs. Aldery, Edmund meets the wounded men who will become family: stammering Private Wren, shell-shocked Captain Ives, and sixteen-year-old drummer boy Tam. Emotional beat: tentative belonging among strangers.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Census taker Mr. Pell's POV. Pell arrives to complete the 1917 register and notices discrepancies: beds counted, names missing, a ledger glimpsed under Edmund's pillow. His suspicion sharpens into obsession as he cross-references parish records by lamplight. Emotional beat: the chill of being watched by bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Names in the Margin
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund reads the ledger aloud to Wren, who finds his brother's name within it, and the house begins treating the book as a shrine of remembrance. Meanwhile Mrs. Aldery warns that Pell has requested military archives. Emotional beat: the ledger transforms from secret burden into shared covenant.

chapters.title: The Berth Counted Twice
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. A telegram announces naval evacuation orders: one boat, limited berths, departure in four days ahead of an expected raid. Tam secretly counts heads against berths and realizes someone will be left behind — and fears it will be him, the least wounded, the most expendable. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Pell's Bargain
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Pell confronts Edmund privately: he will lose his incriminating notes if Edmund surrenders the ledger as evidence of falsified returns. Edmund refuses; Pell threatens to report the whole house as deserters' harbor. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth collide for the first time.

chapters.title: The Vote at Midnight
chapters.summary: Mrs. Aldery's POV. The household votes on who takes the last berth. Each argues for another — Ives for Wren, Wren for Tam, Tam for Edmund — until Mrs. Aldery quietly removes herself from consideration. The vote deadlocks in love rather than rivalry. Emotional beat: found family choosing sacrifice over self.

chapters.title: Raid Tide
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The German shelling begins early; the boat must leave tonight with one berth empty. In the chaos, Pell arrives demanding the ledger, sees the burning horizon, and hesitates between duty and conscience. Emotional beat: terror compressing every prior choice into a single moment.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund gives their own berth to Pell — not as forgiveness but as proof that no name deserves erasure — and presses the ledger into Tam's hands before the boat pulls away through the smoke. Edmund and Mrs. Aldery remain ashore as shells fall. Emotional beat: climax of sacrifice; truth entrusted forward.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, months later. The raid passes; Edmund and Mrs. Aldery survive in the cellars. Saltmere is chartered as an official sanctuary, and on the first registered evening the household reads the ledger aloud, adding new names — including, at Edmund's insistence, Pell's son, lost at sea. Emotional beat: belonging won not by escaping the list but by refusing to let anyone be unnamed.
